animals.Name: Twinkle Toes
animals.Description:
Meet Twinkle Toes. A 7 year old Pittie x lab mix with great house manners and a zest for life. She came to us after being found as a stray in Texas and as soon as you meet her you can tell that she was a well-loved pet. She knows all her basic tricks, doesn't counter surf, and hasn't had a single potty accident with us. She's matured out her puppy energy and just wants a warm home and a best friend to play and go on adventures with.

Her daily routine:

7 am - she dozes away in her dog bed on the floor until I am awake then she patiently waits for me to take her outside by resting her chin on the edge of her bed, staring at me, and wagging her tail. She goes outside for a potty, eats her breakfast, and goes on a walk (10-30 min).

9 am - she stays in her room while I go to work for the day. She's stayed home up to 9 hours outside of her kennel without any potty or chewing incidents.

6 pm - She goes for another walk (10-30 min) and eats dinner.

7 pm - She loves to play with her favorite toy, Froggie. Tug, catch, or just squeaking away on her own. When she's done playing or I have to rescue Froggie from a squeaker-ectomy she curls up in her bed and relaxes for the rest of the night.

10 pm - she has her last potty break and goes to sleep on her bed in my room.

Training:
Twinkle Toes knows the basics: sit, stay, lie down, come, paw, and speak. She's food motivated and can learn new tricks with a bit of patience. She learned to trim her own nails with a scratch board in just a couple of days. She's still working on her leash manners and at the beginning of her walks she usually pulls to explore some sniffs or chase a squirrel. Once she gets some of her excitement out she settles down and walks much more calmly by your side.

Twinkle Toes is wary of strangers and other dogs on leash. She handles moderate foot traffic just fine — it's when people make direct eye contact or approach her that she gets uncomfortable and may bark or growl. She's not aggressive; she's just telling you she needs space. Other dogs on walks are best observed from across the street. With a calm handler who knows how to read the environment and advocate for her, she does great.

Twinkle Toes can get a little too excited sometimes and would prefer a home without cats, rabbits, or other small critters.

If you want to adopt a dog but don't want to start at square one, Twinkle Toes might be perfect for you. Don't let her silver muzzle fool you, Twinkle Toes is young at heart and has plenty of energy and adventures left in her.

animals.Name: Demo
animals.Description:
Demo comes to us from our Alabama partner, where he was found as a stray and then grew up in a shelter. He had minimal human interaction and because of this, Demo needs a patient owner who will let him warm up on his own terms. Demo will do best in a home with another confident dog to learn from and be best buddies with; and a home that has a fenced in yard. Demo is incredibly sweet and kind once he gets to know his humans and will mimic the dog of the house.  You will be able to pet him and give him hugs and he will tell you stories at bedtime reminding you to it’s time to go to bed.  He’s quite the character.

Demo’s foster got him DNA tested using Embark and the results were 32.3% Great Pyrenees, 28.8% American Pit Bull Terrier, 22.3% Supermutt™ (Komondor, Weimaraner, Staffordshire Terrier, Boxer), and 16.6% Anatolian Shepherd.  

Energy Level: Demo is a low- to medium-energy pup who loves to play with all the dogs in his foster home for an hour or two at night (or longer if there’s a high-energy player in the house). He will play whenever another dog wants to, but he is very respectful if they don’t. He is happy to go on a daily walk if you’d like, but he can also take a day off from walking. 

Training: Demo has mostly been learning how to live in a house while in Wisconsin and that his foster mom and visitors are safe. Demo is a major creature of habit. He runs to his kennel for meals. 

Demo also loves scent work and he's really good at it! Livestock guardian dogs have excellent noses! We are only working with one scent right now, vanilla. This is a great training game for him to gain confidence in working with his humans! 

Crate Training: Demo is very food motivated and goes into his kennel easily because he knows he gets meals and treats there. He easily crates all day long next to the resident dog and fellow foster dogs.
Potty Training: Demo is fully potty trained. 

Grooming: Demo has hair similar to a Lab and will need regular brushing due to shedding. 

Dogs: Demo loves every dog in his home. He also goes to doggy daycare and is making new friends there. When he sees another dog across the street while on a walk, he completely ignores them. He also loves every foster that’s come through our house and all the alumni that have come back to stay for a weekend while their parents are out of town.  He’s truly a dog’s dog.

Cats: Demo lives with two cats. They mostly stay upstairs, but when he is around them he gets a bit excited and wants to be best friends. He doesn’t understand that when they run away, they are trying to get away from him.  Demo is an avid sniffer, so cats that don’t like being sniffed by a dog are not a good match for him. 

Demo sleeps upstairs in the bedroom that the cats are in at night with the resident dog and his foster mom to help him bond. He’s doing excellent at learning good behaviors with the cats. He can still get a little nosy though because he loves everyone. 
When we don’t have other fosters the cats are allowed to free roam and Demo is learning to let them be.  Both cats trust him and come out of hiding.

Kids: Demo gets nervous around kids that are the same height as him and will drool, cower and shy away. He has not met teens in my presence. 

People: When Demo meets new people, he follows the resident dog and mirrors their behavior. He is gaining confidence and learning a lot. 

Demo will lie on the couch to hang out with his foster mom and sometimes even snuggles. He loves being on the bed and now allows you to snuggle with him and he’ll even put his face against yours to snuggle in. He’s gaining so much confidence and trust! 

Overall, Demo is an incredibly sweet and goofy boy. He wants everyone to like him but is a little shy at first. Once you are fully accepted into his pack, Demo will sit on you—or another dog. He would do best in a home with another confident dog to learn from, and even better if that dog enjoys playing!

animals.Name: Jane
animals.Description:
Meet Jane! This sweet 3-year-old momma has already raised 11 adorable puppies, and now it’s finally her turn to find a loving forever home. Jane is a wonderful mix of playful energy and couch-potato charm—she’ll happily romp around outside, explore new places, and then curl up beside you for some serious snuggle time. 

Jane is a smart cookie who loves learning new things and enjoys playtime with other dogs, but she’d prefer to be the only dog in the home so she can soak up all the love and attention. Because of her playful style, she would do best in a household with children 12 or older. At about 50 pounds of pure sweetness, Jane is the perfect “play hard, snuggle hard” companion. If you’re looking for a loyal friend who will make you laugh, keep you active, and cuddle up at the end of the day, Jane might just be your girl. Ready to give this deserving mama her happily-ever-after? Jane can’t wait to meet you!

animals.Name: Buddy
animals.Description:
Buddy is a senior cocker spaniel who was surrendered to Fetch when his elderly owner developed health issues and had to go into long term care. He is a happy guy with a big heart, a touch of doggy dementia and the bladder of a polite grandpa.

Buddy absolutely loves other dogs and wants to be near them all the time. He is hard of hearing and doesn’t always notice when other dogs growl at him or don’t want his affection, and he can be a bit persistent with his love, but he responds well if another dog very firmly tells him to leave them alone. Buddy loves his people very much and is always up for attention and snuggles. He is not so good with strangers and will bark loudly when he sees someone he doesn’t know. Sometimes he forgets that he has already met someone and will bark loudly again. He is not a bite risk as he only has a few teeth left (more on that later) but I typically put him in his crate when new people come over so he doesn’t get worked up.

Buddy has some health issues typical of senior dogs. He has a heart murmur that does not currently cause any symptoms and some arthritis that does not keep him from loving his walks and pulling hard on his leash. He has been diagnosed with chronic stenosis of the ear canals so will need to be monitored for ear infections. He also has KCS which is common in smaller breeds and means his eyes do not produce enough tears. He is on an eye ointment twice a day to stimulate tear production and his eyes look perfect now, but he will need to stay on the eye ointment for the rest of his life. He had most of his teeth removed due to severe dental disease, but he still prefers hard kibble to softened food. He can’t chew but he just swallows it whole.

Buddy is mostly good in his crate but he will bark randomly if he wants attention or if he needs to potty, which is about every 2-3 hours during the day. He sleeps in his crate for 9-10 hours at night without a problem. As long as he is let out frequently during the day, he does not have accidents.

If you have a spot in your home for a fuzzy old man who will bark loudly at you for about 10 minutes and then love you forever, come meet Buddy!

animals.Name: Duke
animals.Description:
Meet Duke, a handsome adolescent cattle dog mix with a big personality and the most perfect ears. Duke loves everyone he’s met. He welcomes guests into our house and immediately asks for pets. He also currently lives with two dogs and loves to play with the younger one.

Smart and extremely food-motivated, Duke is easy and fun to train. He apparently thinks kibble is the greatest thing that exists in this world. He has some classic cattle dog traits and adolescent behaviors, so he won’t be the right fit for every home, but for the right family or active individual, he’s an amazing companion.

A day in Duke’s life:

Morning: 45-minute walk to start the day

Playtime with resident dog, then breakfast

Crated during the workday

Evening: yard play, then free in the house with occasional playtime

Dinner

Night: a chew and cozy hanging-out time

Duke’s ideal home is active and consistent, and can provide daily exercise, mental stimulation, and continued training. Duke needs a home that’s more experienced with dogs of his breed mix and age, who can continue to guide him toward becoming a thoughtful adult who makes his own good choices. He can get overexcited when seeing dogs, but would love to live with compatible dogs after a proper introduction and if the dogs are consistently separated for food, as he can guard meals and chews. If you’re looking for a loyal, smart, and affectionate buddy and are ready for a lively young cattle-dog mix, Duke could be your perfect match.

animals.Name: Diamond
animals.Description:
Meet Princess Diamond: A Snuggly, Dazzling Girl Looking for Her Forever Home!

Diamond is one of the most affectionate dogs you’ll be lucky to meet. Though she needs patient introductions to new humans, she adores every human her foster family has brought into her circle! Diamond is a cuddly girl, and loves to lay on top of you or by your feet. Your heart will melt when she rests her chin on your chest.  She will bond deeply with whoever is lucky enough to adopt her.

Rescued in Arkansas, Diamond spent several months with a local rescue before making her way to the Midwest. She’s adapted exceptionally well to Wisconsin living!

Diamond is polite and relaxed inside her home. She rarely barks, never chews on items she shouldn’t, and loves to laze around in her favorite cozy spots! She has never shown any kind of resource guarding with humans, and is gentle when taking treats. She loves toys and will happily play fetch or tug with her humans.

Diamond is fully potty-trained and crate-trained. She’s never had an accident inside the house. Diamond is a smart girl and will go into her crate on command! She will happily snooze in her crate for up to 4 hours at a time. Diamond can also be left to free-roam.

Diamond walks well on leash, and prefers leisurely strolls with lots of sniffing and joyful rolling in the grass. She’s a curious girl, and will occasionally lunge at a squirrel or bird. Diamond is working through leash reactivity towards other pups, but can be redirected with treats.

Because of her past behavior towards other dogs, Diamond must be the only pet in her home. This is ideal so she can give you all her love and attention!

Diamond would do well in an adult-only home or in a home with older, quieter kids.

Diamond is looking for a loving adopter who is willing to take things slowly as she adjusts to her new home. If you're the kind of person who appreciates a sweet, affectionate dog with a big heart, Diamond is the dog for you.

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Nellie
animals.Description:
Nellie is a gentle, soulful foxhound who’s made an incredible journey from scared and fragile to quietly brave and loving. When she was rescued, she was underweight, injured, and too frightened to trust—but with patience, she’s grown into a healthy 50-pound girl who now seeks out affection and melts into her people 🧡. She can still be a little shy at first, but once she feels safe, her sweet personality shines through in the softest, most heart-melting ways.
She loves simple things: long sniffy walks, fresh air, and being near her humans. A secure fence is a must (her nose will lead her on adventures!), and she’s still building confidence being alone, but she’s making steady progress. Nellie doesn’t ask for much—just love and patience—but in return, she gives a deep, loyal bond and the kind of quiet companionship that feels really special.

animals.Name: Max
animals.Description:
Max is a beautiful 2 year old Siberian husky who was surrendered due to his owner’s family health issues. He is a happy, friendly guy who is potty trained, crate trained and knows basic commands (although whether he chooses to listen or is distracted by his husky brain is another story lol - but if you have food, he will ALWAYS listen!). He gets along great with other dogs but gets a little too excited about cats and wants to chase them. Max is very chill for a husky and spends most of the day sleeping, although he does enjoy going out in the yard and exploring the fence line. He loves to get pets and rub up against you. If he wants attention he will talk to you as huskies do until you notice him.

Max has idiopathic epilepsy and takes seizure medications twice a day. He is in the process of switching to a new medication that should better control his type of seizures. His goal is to have a seizure no more than once every few months, but he will likely never be completely seizure free. His adopters will need to be aware and comfortable with that. His meds make him drink a lot of water, so he has to pee a lot. He would do best with someone who is home most of the time and able to let him out.

If you are looking for a dog who is past the puppy stage but still young enough to be your buddy for many years, Max is your guy!

animals.Name: Amara
animals.Description: Amara is a smart sweet 11 month pup.  Although she's  in her grown up body at a svelte 57 pounds, she still a puppy at heart and sometimes those zoomies just need to get out.  She doesn't  always have zoomies under control and sometimes we get soooo excited we must greet you with a jump, we are working on it, but because of this, we would recommend  a household with no small children under 12.   She would love a fenced yard to show off her speed.   Amara is house trained and crate trained.  She sleeps in the bedroom on the floor and just wants to be with you.  Amara would benefit from more socialization and slow introductions.  Amara is extremely  food motivated and learns fast, although she does have a bit of an independent streak at times.  She would shine in a forever home committed to working on her training, with a little patience and some kibble, she could soon be "Dog of the Year."

animals.Name: Stacy
animals.Description:
Stacy: Your Dog’s Very Own Cat-Dog Hybrid (Now in a shorter, sillier edition)
Looking for a cat for your dog? Perfect. Stacy has arrived to fill that extremely niche job.

Sweet, tiny Stacy is basically a travel‑sized Great Pyrenees with the soul of a mildly judgmental house cat. She and her brother Demo started life on the streets of Alabama, then somehow ended up in Wisconsin, where she now supervises humans with quiet disapproval.

She’s gentle, quirky, shy at first, and absolutely convinced she is cooler than everyone. Stacy loves affection—after she decides you deserve it. She does not follow you everywhere, for she has important cat‑dog business to attend to.

Her favorite things:
* Her dog friends (non‑negotiable—she needs at least one).
* Butt wiggles that appear without warning.
* Randomly showing up with a stick in her mouth, peeking around the corner like she’s checking if you’re busy.
* Making ridiculous faces that seem designed to make you laugh.
* Acting like a cat who accidentally downloaded the “dog” expansion pack.

She’s house trained, walks beautifully on leash, and can free‑roam like a tiny, furry landlord. Quiet, polite, expressive, and occasionally smirky—Stacy is 72% dog, 28% cat, and 100% cute weirdo.

Stacy is looking for:
* A patient human who understands shy dogs.
* A calm home where she can bloom.
* A friendly dog buddy to be her emotional-support extrovert.
* Someone who appreciates cat energy in a dog body.
If you’ve ever said, “I want a cat… but also a dog,” congratulations. Stacy is your girl.

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone
⚠ Needs another dog in the home

animals.Name: Ruthie
animals.Description:
Meet Ruthie — the wiggliest, chaos‑powered sunshine noodle of a dog.
Ruthie greets life like it’s a talent show and she’s performing “Extreme Wiggles, Interpretive Edition.” Her tail spins like a tiny helicopter, her smile is pure mischief, and she fully believes humans exist for belly rubs. If you stop petting her, she’ll gently paw at you like, “Hello??? Customer service??? I ordered affection.”
She’s a joyful, affectionate girl who loves outdoor adventures, walkies, sunshine, and rolling under the covers like a gremlin who just discovered slapstick comedy. Ruthie was found pregnant on the streets of Alabama before making her way to Wisconsin, where she raised the famous “pasta puppy” litter — because of course the goofiest dog also makes the cutest babies.
Ruthie LOVES being outside. She LOVES her people. She LOVES being goofy. She LOVES belly rubs. Honestly, she’s just out here living her best sitcom‑dog life.
She’s eager to please, enjoys learning, and has the kind of personality that makes strangers say, “Oh my gosh, look at her!” right before falling in love. She’s been treated for heartworm and is feeling better every day.
If you’re a human who wants a built‑in adventure buddy with maximum wiggle power, Ruthie is ready to trot into your life and dramatically flop onto your lap for rubs.

animals.Name: Moka
animals.Description:
Moka is a calm, low-energy sweetheart looking for a peaceful home where she can relax and enjoy life. She's incredibly well-mannered, smart, and easy to live with, making her a wonderful companion for someone looking for a laid-back pup.

One of Moka's favorite things is spending time with her people—especially if belly rubs are involved! She also enjoys car rides and is always happy to tag along for an adventure.

Moka has previously lived with another dog and seems to be most confident when she has a canine companion by her side. She would love a home with another calm, low-key dog to keep her company and help her feel secure.

She is fully potty trained and has never had an accident in her foster home. Moka free roams the house during the day without getting into anything, but she's also perfectly happy to settle into her crate if asked. She has excellent house manners and already knows several commands, including sit, down, stay, leave it, and comes when calling her name.

Moka can be sensitive to loud noises when she's outside, although they don't seem to bother her indoors. Because of this, she'd thrive in a quieter neighborhood with a lower-activity lifestyle. This would also be ideal for her because of a pre-existing knee injury. Moka has a dislocated kneecap from an injury she sustained when she was younger, but with joint supplements and moderate exercise, she manages it well and continues to enjoy life.

If you're looking for a gentle, loving, and well-behaved companion who will happily keep you company, join you for a leisurely car ride, and soak up all the belly rubs you have to offer, Moka could be the perfect addition to your life.

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Pete
animals.Description:
Pete is a shy beagle who's still building his trust in people—but he's making progress. Right now, he feels safest with his canine pack mates and prefers to spend most of his time with them. He doesn't readily trust people, but he's slowly learning that humans can be okay, and that's huge growth for this sensitive guy.

Getting picked up takes Pete a moment to adjust—he'll need some time to settle and feel secure—but once he relaxes, he's willing to accept your gentle touch and affection. He's learning that patience and kindness lead to good things.

Pete is a work in progress, and he needs a home that understands his pace. He thrives best without the unpredictability and noise of young children right now, though with time and the right environment, he may warm up to them. What he needs most is consistency, the companionship of another dog who can model confidence, and patience as he learns to trust.

What Pete needs:

A patient, calm family committed to his slow progress
A fenced-in yard for safe, low-pressure exploration
At least one dog friend who can help model trust and confidence
A home without young children at this stage
Time and quiet spaces to decompress and build trust at his own pace

If you have the patience to let Pete bloom at his own speed, you'll discover what a sweet, gentle soul he is.

animals.Name: Callie
animals.Description:
Callie is a sweet, easy-going girl looking for a loving new home after her owner moved into a nursing home. She can be a little cautious when meeting new people, but she warms up quickly and becomes very affectionate once she feels comfortable.

Callie is indifferent to other dogs and has done well free-roaming alongside a calm canine companion, but she would also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home. She is gentle with children, though because she can be startled by loud noises and sudden movements, she would be happiest in a quieter home.

Callie is currently overweight, so she's not up for long hikes or strenuous adventures—especially in the summer heat. Instead, she enjoys leisurely walks, chewing on her favorite toys, and curling up for long naps (either on the cool floor or the couch). 
She is quiet, trustworthy, and does well free-roaming in an apartment. She is afraid of the apartment elevators, so she just takes the stairs at this time.

Callie would make an excellent companion for a first-time dog owner looking for a loyal, easy-going, affectionate best friend.

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Benedict
animals.Description:
Benedict is a shy, sweet boy who’s still learning that the world isn’t as scary as it feels. So far, he’s been the kind of dog who watches quietly from the sidelines, taking everything in with those soft, thoughtful eyes. Once he trusts you, his whole body relaxes and you get to see the tender, loyal heart underneath.

Benedict absolutely thrives with another dog in the home. A confident canine friend helps him feel safe, shows him the ropes, and reminds him that good things are coming. He’s also perfectly fine with cats and coexists with them politely.

Leashes? Benedict has no idea what those are yet. He’ll need patience, gentle guidance, and a calm environment while he learns. The good news is he rides beautifully in the car, settling in quietly and taking comfort in the steady routine of travel.

Benedict is looking for an adopter who understands shy dogs - someone who won’t rush him, who celebrates small victories, and who can offer a peaceful home with a friendly dog to show him the way. With time, kindness, and stability, Benedict will blossom into the devoted companion he’s meant to be.

If you’re the kind of person who finds magic in the quiet ones, Benedict is ready to meet you.

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Turtle
animals.Description:
Turtle may sound slow and steady, but this little guy is full of gentle curiosity, soft affection, and bursts of goofy puppy energy that make him impossible not to love.

He adores exploring his world one bouncy step at a time, then suddenly zooming off with a toy when inspiration strikes. Turtle is learning, growing, and discovering his confidence, and he’s already showing how deeply he bonds with the people who care for him. Whether he’s striking a dramatic pose, trotting over with his tail wagging, or curling up for quiet snuggles, Turtle brings joy in every moment.

He’s smart, social, and wonderfully tender‑hearted — the perfect mix of silly and sweet. Turtle is ready for a forever home that will appreciate his thoughtful nature, encourage his playful side, and help him blossom into the loving companion he’s meant to be.

If you’re looking for a puppy who will brighten your days, warm your heart, and grow with your family, Turtle is ready to wiggle his way in.

animals.Name: Skye
animals.Description:
Skye is a sweet, affectionate girl with a soft heart and an endless amount of love for her people. At 7 years old, she has traded the puppy chaos for the sweeter things in life, being close to her humans, enjoying a comfortable routine, and running around to play to her heart’s content.

True to her Blue Heeler genes, she has energy to spare and jumps for joy at the opportunity to chase after squirrels outside.

Skye is the kind of dog who loves deeply and forms a special bond with the people she trusts. She enjoys being included in everyday life and is happiest simply knowing her person is close. Whether she’s joining you for a walk, keeping you company around the house, or winding down beside you at the end of the day, Skye makes an easy and loving companion.

Changes can take time for Skye to adjust to, and being away from her people can sometimes make her nervous. Skye can also show some jealousy or frustration toward other dogs, especially when attention or treats are being shared, so she would do best with thoughtful introductions and a family who can help her feel secure. 

With patience, consistency, and plenty of love, she settles in and lets her sweet, loyal, personality shine. Skye would thrive with someone who appreciates a dog with a tender heart and wants a companion to truly become part of their every day life. She’ll reward that person with affection, loyalty, and the kind of companionship that makes a house feel a little more like home.

Skye is ready to bring adventure, love, and plenty of cuddles to her forever home.

animals.Name: Simon Says
animals.Description:
Meet ✨Simon✨, the only dog who comes with a FREE emotional support slinky named Stan. That's right—you get a two-for-one deal. 

Stan is Simon's prized possession. He proudly carries him around the house, shows him off to anyone willing to admire his handsome friend, and even insists on taking Stan outside for little strolls. We don't ask questions. We just accept that Stan is family.

Simon originally came to Fetch from northern Wisconsin after his beloved owner passed away. While his life took an unexpected turn, he hasn't let it dim his sweet, goofy spirit.

This handsome guy is as easygoing as they come. He's calm, affectionate, wonderful with people, gets along great with other animals, and firmly believes snacks solve most problems. He's playful without being wild, loves attention, and greets life with the happiest little tippy-tappies you've ever seen.

The Labrador in Simon is impossible to miss. If there's water nearby, he's in it. Lakes? Yes. Kiddie pools? Absolutely. Mud puddles? If you're not looking... probably.

Simon isn't looking for anything fancy. Just a family to love, treats to politely accept, water to splash in, and plenty of opportunities to proudly parade Stan around like the tiny celebrity he is.

Adopt Simon and you'll get one incredible dog... plus Stan, his slightly floppy but very important sidekick.

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Carlos
animals.Description:
Carlos (aka Ham Bone) comes in a tiny, yet chunky, package FULL of personality. His previous fosters described him as the class clown.
He’s not so interested in toys as he is in people. He wants to be close and get all the scratches from everyone he meets.
Carlos is house trained and would likely do well free roaming in a home once he’s acclimated. He currently has the run of his own room. He may complain a bit when separated, but he settles very quickly.
Carlos lives with a dog sibling, but ignores him for the most part.
Carlos doesn’t need a whole lot of exercise. He moves at a high speed in very small burrata, giving him the appearance of a silly windup toy.
Carlos is easy peasy and would love a forever person to love and snuggle.

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Cain
animals.Description:
Meet Cain, a striking black-and-white mixed breed with a heart as big as his smile! At just 8 months old and 41 pounds, this handsome parvo survivor has already overcome a tough start and is ready to find the loving family he's been waiting for.

Cain is an affectionate, playful pup who loves spending time with his people. Whether he's exploring on a walk, chasing a tennis ball in the backyard, or sneaking in a kiss, he's happiest when he's part of the action. He gets along well with other active dogs and would enjoy a playmate who can match his energy.

He's house trained, walks nicely on leash, and is a dream in his crate, sleeping quietly through the night without a fuss. Cain is eager to learn and enjoys practicing new skills. He's currently working on sit, down, and touch, and would love a family that will continue building his confidence and skills through training.

Like most teenage pups, Cain is still figuring out his manners. He can get a little mouthy or jump up when he's excited, but he's easily redirected and improves with consistency.

Cain's ideal home is one that enjoys staying active and will include him in daily walks, games of fetch, and plenty of quality time together. In return, you'll get a loyal companion with a goofy personality, a loving heart, and a lifetime of adventures ahead. 🐶 🐮

animals.Name: Malibu
animals.Description:
Malibu is a sweet, friendly girl with a heart full of love and a tail that never stops wagging. She loves spending time with her people and is happiest when she's by your side, whether that's playing in the yard, going for a walk, or snuggling up after a fun day.

This happy pup has a playful spirit and enjoys making new friends, both human and canine. Malibu's affectionate personality and gentle nature make her a wonderful companion for a family, couple, or individual looking for a loyal best friend.

If you're searching for a loving, playful pup who will fill your days with joy, Malibu may be the perfect match for you. Come meet her and see why everyone falls in love with this sweet girl! ❤️🐶

animals.Name: Lily
animals.Description:
Meet Lily!

If you're looking for a sweet, gentle companion with a heart full of love, Lily just might be your perfect match.

Lily has never met a dog she didn't like! She has been friendly with every dog she's encountered and would likely love having a canine brother or sister to romp around with. I think she gets a little bored with just me sometimes and would really enjoy having a playmate.

She also absolutely adores people. Walks with Lily are more of a leisurely "sniffari" than a power walk because she's convinced every smell is worth investigating—and every person deserves a friendly hello! She's wonderful on a leash and is happy to take her time exploring the world.

One of Lily's best qualities is how easygoing she is. She hardly ever barks (I've only heard her "talk" a couple of times), she's respectful during mealtimes and doesn't beg for food, and if you tell her "no," she'll simply lie down and relax. At bedtime, she's happiest curled up next to her person and will happily sleep in as long as you do.

Lily also does well with grooming appointments and will happily head into her crate—as long as there's a tasty treat waiting for her!

Like any young dog, Lily is still learning. She's making wonderful progress with potty training (we've even had two perfect days in a row!), but she'll need a family that's patient as she learns to let you know when she needs to go outside. She's also figuring out what's appropriate to chew, so keeping an eye on rugs, pillows, remotes, and other tempting treasures is important. She's working on basic commands like sit, stay, and come, and while car rides aren't her favorite yet, I think she'll gain confidence with a little more experience.

One thing to know about Lily is that she occasionally gets the zoomies! They're adorable to watch, but because she's a bigger girl, she could accidentally knock over a small child during one of her bursts of excitement.

Lily is a loving, affectionate dog with a gentle spirit who's looking for a family willing to continue teaching her the ropes. In return, you'll get a loyal best friend who loves people, gets along beautifully with other dogs, and will happily be your shadow through every sniff-filled walk and cozy morning cuddle.

If you're ready to open your heart to a wonderful girl who's already well on her way to becoming an amazing family dog, Lily is ready to meet you.

animals.Name: Rosie
animals.Description:
Rosie is a lively gal with a joyful spirit and a heart full of love. At 10 years old, she’s the perfect mix of seasoned sweetness and surprising pep; a senior in age, but absolutely not in attitude.

Rosie still loves her walks, playtime, and exploring the yard. She’s the kind of dog who greets each day with a happy tail and a little bounce. She adores her people and happily leans in for pets, cuddles, and attention.

Poodles are famously clever, and Rosie is no exception. She enjoys learning, sniffing games, and anything that engages her brain - ESPECIALLY when food is involved. 

Rosie loves regular walks and bursts of play. She’s not a hyper dog, but she definitely isn’t slowing down yet. She enjoys being around people and has lived with dogs, cats, and kiddos. After her adventures, she’s all about soft beds, warm blankets, and curling up near her favorite humans.

Rosie would thrive with someone who appreciates a dog that’s both cuddly and spirited. She’d be a great match for adults, families, or anyone who wants a companion who’s always ready for a walk, a game, or a cozy evening together. Rosie brings joy, loyalty, and a spark of fun wherever she goes. She’s looking for a home that will celebrate her energy, cherish her sweetness, and give her the love she’s been waiting for.

Attributes.AttributeName: Has many approved adopters waiting to meet them!

animals.Name: Maya
animals.Description: May 4, 2026Meet Maya, a 51-pound "lap dog" who hasn’t quite looked at a tape measure lately! At three years old, this Australian Kelpie mix is the perfect blend of sweetness and soul.Maya is the definition of "medium energy"—she’s always up for an adventurous neighborhood stroll to take in the sights and smells, but she’s just as happy to clock out for a professional-grade snuggle session. Despite her size, her favorite place in the world is right on top of you; she’s a world-class cuddler who truly believes she fits perfectly in any lap.If you’re looking for a lovable, amazing companion who is as gentle as she is loyal, Maya is ready to move right in and steal your heart (and your seat on the couch).

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Birdie
animals.Description:
Birdie is the sweetest, snuggliest girl! After spending much of her life as a stray and raising six puppies of her own, she's more than ready to enjoy the good life in a loving forever home. Her favorite place to be is right next to her person, whether that's curled up on the couch for cuddles or following you from room to room.

Birdie has made lots of progress adjusting to indoor life and is nearly fully potty trained. She sleeps soundly through the night in her crate or snuggled up in bed with her foster parents, and seems to do well when left home alone in her crate. As she keeps learning the ropes of being a family dog, Birdie will benefit from continued basic training and guidance. Like many Chihuahuas, she can be vocal, though she's making progress with gentle redirection and reassurance from her foster family.

Birdie has done well being around adults, older children, cats, and other dogs. She currently lives with another dog in her foster home. Birdie can be nervous around new people, but once you've won her over, she is all snuggles and kisses ♥️

Because Birdie forms strong bonds, she can be a little anxious when her favorite person leaves. Fortunately, this seems to be greatly improving as she settles into her foster home. 

Her ideal adopter will be patient, understanding, and willing to continue helping her feel secure and independent.

If you're looking for a loving companion who will adore you with her whole heart, Birdie just might be your perfect match.

animals.Name: Mary Beth
animals.Description:
Mary Beth is the kind of dog who makes friends everywhere she goes. This sweet girl is full of love and generous with her kisses, always happy to show her people just how much she cares. She is incredibly attentive to humans and loves being part of whatever you're doing, whether that's heading out for a walk or spending a quiet afternoon relaxing at home.
Mary Beth is dog-friendly and enjoys the company of other dogs. Her story began in Alabama, where she was found as a stray while pregnant. After lovingly raising her puppies—the "Plant Puppies" who are currently available for adoption—it's finally Mary Beth's turn to find a family of her own.
She loves walks, thrives on companionship, and is ready to be someone's loyal best friend. After giving so much love to her puppies, Mary Beth deserves a home where she can be cherished just as much. If you're looking for a sweet, affectionate companion who will happily share life's everyday moments with you, Mary Beth may be the perfect fit. ❤️

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Sheila
animals.Description:
Sheila is a tiny Shih Tzu who may look like a classic “easy lap dog,” but she is not that dog right now. She came from a breeding/hoarding situation in Texas, and her world has always been small, loud, and scary. Because of that, she is extremely nervous and fearful and she will need an adopter who understands trauma, patience, and slow progress.
What she’s like today:
• Very fearful of people. She does not currently allow petting and will retreat to her crate when she feels overwhelmed. After a few weeks with us, she will come forward to sniff us, which is a small but meaningful step.
• Not leash ready. She cannot be walked outside or walked on a leash at this time. She has extreme panic when placed on a leash or with outdoor exposure.
• Pee pad trained. She uses pads reliably and rarely has accidents off them.
• Her crate is her safe space. She sleeps and decompresses there, running to her crate whenever she is afraid or overwhelmed. She likes to gather her toys inside.
• Loves toys. She quietly plays, collects them, and occasionally shows flashes of “real dog” joy—tail chasing, play bows, little bursts of silliness.
• Kid friendly in the sense that she ignores them. She lives with dog-savvy, animal compassionate kids (8, 13, 15) but does not interact with them.
• Would benefit from another calm, friendly dog. She watches other dogs closely and would likely learn from a confident, gentle companion.
Who she needs:
She needs someone who can offer grace, time, and zero pressure. She is not going to be a cuddly companion anytime soon. She is not ready for walks, dog parks, or social outings. She is a long term project—tiny and adorable, yes, but emotionally complex and still learning what safety feels like.
If you are patient, trauma informed, and willing to celebrate very small victories, she has the potential to grow into a much braver version of herself. She is slowly coming out of her shell, and with the right home, those little glimpses of joy can become the norm rather than tiny moments.
Sheila isn’t an easy dog, but she is a diamond in the rough and deserves all the love and joy in her life.

animals.Name: Belle
animals.Description: Meet Belle a bundle of happiness! This little furball is full of puppy kisses, playful antics, and endless cuddles. She is curious, affectionate, and eager to find a family to call her own. Whether it's playtime, nap time, or cuddle time, Belle is always happy to be by your side. Are you ready to welcome this adorable pup into your heart and home? ❤️🐾

animals.Name: Emma
animals.Description:
Emma is a bright‑eyed, bushy tailed cattle dog with a heart full of devotion and a mind that never stops working. She’s the kind of dog who notices everything, loves deeply, and brings a quiet spark of energy into every room she enters.

True to her cattle dog roots, she’s clever, alert, and always ready for a job or a puzzle. Emma thrives on regular exercise, enrichment games, and time outdoors. She loves being near her humans and is happiest when she’s included in family life. She responds beautifully to positive training and enjoys learning new cues.

Emma will make you laugh, keep you moving, and reward you with unwavering loyalty. If you’re looking for a dog who’s as loving as she is spirited, Emma is ready to meet you.

animals.Name: Marigold
animals.Description: Marigold was surrendered from an Amish farm where she was used for breeding. She is shy but very sweet and will wag her tail at everyone and cautiously come up for pets. She is learning housetraining and walking on a leash. She loves other dogs and is very friendly and submissive with my pack. Marigold is a nonshedding dog and will need regular haircuts. She was very matted when we picked her up and had to be completely shaved, but she will be very cute and fluffy when her hair grows out! She is a rare straight-haired bichon, not the typical curly coat.

animals.Name: Cash
animals.Description:
Good with dogs, Good with kids, Good with Cats, House trained, Can free roam, Walks well on leash, Good in car, Senior Dog, Crate Trained, Friendly

Older dapper gent seeks connection for next phase of life. Meet Cash - he's a gentle sweetheart who's looking for the next love of his life following the passing of his previous human. 

Cash is an easy going guy. He's friendly to every adult/child/dog/cat we've met - either politely greeting them or simply ignoring them and letting them be. He's a real people person and likes to follow his favorite gal around the house (he seems to connect more with women we've found - likes men, but a Velcro dog for women), but when left alone he settles onto his dog bed and patiently waits for your return.

Being an older guy he's got things down. He knows when it's potty time or will let you know he needs to head out - he's got a great old man bark. He walks well on leash; no tugging or lunging at small animals. He loves a good car ride - head out the window! He's great in public; we took him to various breweries during his first week here and he couldn't have been better. Being older also has some challenges - he's got some hip pain/arthritis and needs a daily med/supplement. He has trouble getting into a car - we've been introducing him to a ramp, but he's not a huge fan, so there's some lifting in and out.

General day for Cash:
6:30 am: Wake up and first big walk of the. "Big" is relative; we don't go far - he's got some hip issues so we take a nice slow walk. He knows it is time to potty and gets his business done. A few blocks is all he needs.

7am food (and joint supplement/med) He takes his meds very easily with some peanut butter.

Then he'll either go to work with me or we stay home and work from home. Cash is happy to visit the office and see people. Then he'll settle down and let me work. 

12 noon food. And potty break - very short.

More patiently waiting while work is done. A potty break if needed.

5pm: Day is done. Second big walk (again "big" here is pretty small).

Pets and play time, settles near us if we're home. If we go out he's good about being alone.

7pm food (and joint supplement/med)

9:30 pm: Last walk of the night. Upon return - dentastix and bed time. We let him sleep outside the kennel. He did fine in it, but we thought it was uncomfortable for his hips (and he's so well behaved) that we just let him free roam in the family room and sleep on a dog bed by the patio door.

If you're looking for a sweet, older guy to enjoy slow, short walks and nice quiet sitting you gotta meet Cash.

animals.Name: Whiskey
animals.Description:
Whiskey is a spunky beagle who's still figuring out what it means to be a house dog—and he's making great progress! He's currently learning the ropes while living with three other dogs, and those furry friends have become his best teachers.

This young guy is a bouncy adolescent with plenty of energy to burn. He's a bit shy at first and takes time to warm up to people, but once he trusts you, he's got a sweet side—pick him up and he'll happily settle in for a nap on your lap. He thrives on companionship and needs a home where he can continue learning alongside a confident, well-adjusted dog. With the right mentor and patient humans by his side, Whiskey's confidence grows every day.

What Whiskey needs:

A fenced-in yard for safe play and exploration
A patient family willing to support his continued growth
At least one dog friend who can model good behavior
Love, consistency, and plenty of opportunities to be part of the pack

If you have a stable home with another dog and the patience to watch Whiskey blossom, he's ready to return all that investment with the loyal companionship only a beagle can offer.

animals.Name: Sugar
animals.Description:
Sugar is looking for a new home because she does not get along with the neighbor’s dog and it is unsafe for them to live near each other. It is unclear why she doesn’t like this particular dog because she is typically very friendly and submissive with other dogs. She goes to doggy daycare and boarding and has never had an issue with any of the dogs there.

Hi. Yes, hello. I’m the dog.

My name is Sugar, and apparently I’m writing my own profile because my human says I’m looking for a new home — preferably one with soft blankets, snacks, and humans who appreciate world-class cuddling.

About Me: 
Strong (emotionally and physically
Loyal to my people
The sweetest girl — cuddling is basically my full-time job
Excellent at reminding humans they should go outside more
Professional greeter who acts like you’ve been gone for years (even if you just got groceries)

My Personality Resume:
Loves MOST dogs
Super sweet with kids and all strangers — people are my favorite
Never growled at or been afraid of humans
No chewing your stuff or counter surfing (I have manners)
Comfortable in my kennel, but will happily sleep under the blankets if invited
Takes neighborhood wildlife patrol very seriously (squirrels, birds, rabbits beware)
Cats and I are not compatible roommates

What I’m Looking For:
• A confident human comfortable handling a strong dog
• Someone who enjoys walks, fresh air, and unconditional love
• A home where I can be part of the family (and possibly the bed)

My current human loves me very much, but life changes mean they want to find me the best possible forever home where I can thrive and keep being my sweet, happy self.

If you’re looking for a loyal companion, built-in walking buddy, and professional snuggler… I might be your girl.
Apply within. Treats encouraged.

animals.Name: Bailey
animals.Description: With sadness I am looking to rehome my 9-year-old black lab mix Bailey. He has no health issues, is up to date on his vaccines, and has quite a bit of energy for a "senior" dog. I've had him for five and a half years and recently had children. It turns out that young children really stress Bailey out. He is great in a kid-free or older kid home, and I think he would be happier and less stressed spending his remaining years in that environment. Like all dogs, he has his quirks which I'm happy to discuss more if you are interested. Things that would come with Bailey include: 1-2 months of food and treats, stainless steel water and food bowls, kennel, toys, and leash/collars.

animals.Name: Buddy the Hound
animals.Description: Buddy is looking for a new home after his owner passed away. He is currently being cared for by a family member but she is unable to continue caring for him due to her own health issues. Buddy is a loving, snuggly boy who loves to follow you around. He is potty trained and crate trained. He is currently living in an apartment and does great as long as he gets a good amount of exercise.

Attributes.AttributeName: ✅ Can free roam when humans are gone

animals.Name: Sabo
animals.Description:
Sabo is an incredibly fun-loving, sweet little guy who loves more than anything to be outdoors. If he could spend his life outside all the time he would, but he comes inside when he's done playing because he knows that's where he gets to cuddle up to his people on the couch. And don't you dare stop petting him during a cuddle-session, he takes personal offense to that; he will sweetly nudge your hand and worm his way into your lap for more belly scratches. 

With how much Sabo loves to explore with his nose to the ground, he would love someone who takes him on LOTS of hiking and/or walking adventures. Sometimes he gets such an intense adventure-itch that he doesn't wait and digs his way out from under the fence to go explore, but he always comes back after a while. 

Sabo is house trained, but has a small bladder so if someone is extra late letting him out on his schedule, he may have an accident in the house. 

Sabo is great with other dogs, but may need some supervision around small dogs and cats because sometimes he doesn't respect their space and needs correcting because he's still learning that not everyone wants to play with him, and sometimes he just lacks spacial awareness and accidentally tramples smaller animals in his excitement. He has never been aggressive toward any dogs or cats, but has not had exposure to any other domestic animals. 

He is very respectful when dogs his size or bigger set a boundary, and as long as he has toys/chews he's pretty good at keeping himself entertained for periods of time. 

Sabo needs more work on his leash manners,  recall, crate-training, jumping, digging out of the fence, and putting paws on the edge of the kitchen counter to smell what you're cooking. Also, if he is left alone with no toys or chews, he may find something he shouldn't be chewing on to keep entertained. 

He is VERY food motivated, which helps tremendously with training, but also means he needs to be fed with supervision, or separately from other pets so that he doesn't steal their food. He is fine with eating meals in a crate. 

For only a medium size dog, Sabo contains so much joy and spirit, and when he finds his outdoors-loving owner we know with some more training he will be the perfect companion for them, and they will have wonderful adventures together!

animals.Name: Morgan Riley
animals.Description: Morgan Riley is a 5 y/o Bernedoodle and is being surrendered due to family health issues. He is a very happy boy and loves  to play with other dogs. He plays rough and can be vocal, but he is just playing. He loves to play catch with balls and frisbee. He is housebroken, crate trained and loves to take naps. He loves to have his back scratched and belly rubbed. He watches TV when animals are on and talks to them. He is very strong and does jump on people to greet them when he gets excited. He has not been around many children, but loves all adults. He will definitely make someone a great pet.

animals.Name: Rockelle
animals.Description:
Rockelle, at just 2½ months old, this beautiful terrier mix puppy is already stealing hearts with her confident personality and sweet nature. Weighing in at 21 pounds, she's going to be a big girl! One of her unique features is the double dew claws on her back paws, a trait often associated with Catahoula Leapord dogs (Her brothers have that coloring). Due to the potty training progress, sleeping through the night and general demeanor, I think she is closer to 4 months (I have fostered over 45 puppies).

This happy pup is doing very well with potty training and is already comfortable in her crate, making the transition into her new home even easier. She is incredibly social, loves meeting new people, and genuinely enjoys being with her family. She seeks out her people for companionship and affection and is happiest when she's included in the fun.

She has spent time playing with my 2-, 3-, and 10-year-old grandchildren and was wonderful with all of them. She's gentle, playful, and knows how to have fun without being too rough. She also loves her toys and plays with them appropriately, happily entertaining herself or inviting you to join in.
This little girl is confident, curious, and eager to explore the world. She approaches new experiences with enthusiasm and has the kind of outgoing personality that makes her a joy to be around. Whether she's playing, cuddling, or following you from room to room, she is always ready to be part of whatever you're doing.

If you're looking for a smart, affectionate, well-socialized puppy with a delightful personality and the potential to grow into a loyal, loving companion, this special girl may be the perfect addition to your family.

animals.Name: Creed
animals.Description:
At just 2½ months old, this adorable puppy is already showing what a wonderful companion he's going to be. Weighing 17 pounds at his young age, he's going to be a big boy! While his looks and personality point to a mix of Catahoula Leopard Dog or Australian Cattle Dog . Due to the potty training progress, sleeping through the night and general demeanor, I think he is closer to 4 months (I have fostered over 45 puppies).

This sweet boy is doing very well with potty training and is comfortable relaxing in his crate, making him off to a great start in life. While he's a little more reserved when meeting new people than his sister, he warms up quickly and enjoys spending time with people of all ages. He has done wonderfully with my 2-, 3-, and 10-year-old grandchildren, showing a gentle, patient nature. He can be a little noisy when first crated or when playing with another dog. He settles shortly after I leave. 

He also gets along very well with other dogs and enjoys having canine companions to play with. He loves playing with toys and does so appropriately, happily entertaining himself or joining in when it's playtime.
This handsome pup has a calm confidence about him. He's curious without being overly bold and enjoys exploring his surroundings at his own pace. Once he knows you're his person, he's affectionate and loyal, seeking out your company and enjoying being part of the family.

If you're looking for a smart, gentle, well-socialized puppy with a sweet disposition and the potential to grow into a devoted lifelong companion, this special boy is ready to find his forever home.
